hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: A household's recent purchasing behaviour (spend in trailing windows, trip frequency, recency, momentum between aligned lag windows) predicts its next 4-week spend better than demographics alone.
transformation_description: Added 18 behavioural features computed from transactions up to each snapshot: spend in 28/56/84/112/364-day trailing windows, two aligned 28-day lag windows, trip counts, average basket, active days, tenure, recency, lifetime spend/trips/rate, trend and lag ratio.
reasoning_summary: Recent spend and trip cadence are the most direct predictors of near-future spend; momentum features capture whether spend is rising or falling.

hypothesis: Marketing exposure and promotion/assortment mix predict future spend: households targeted by more campaigns (especially TypeA), recent coupon redeemers, high discount users, private-brand buyers, and department mix (fresh/produce share) will spend differently in the next 4 weeks.
transformation_description: Added 20 features to E001: campaign targeting counts by type + active-campaign flag + days since campaign start; coupon redemption counts/recency; discount share of spend (28d); private-brand share and 8 department spend shares (84d).
reasoning_summary: Campaign targeting and coupon activity proxy marketing responsiveness and engagement; discount/private-brand/dept mix captures price sensitivity and basket composition, all plausibly linked to future spend levels.

hypothesis: What a household buys (department mix, private-brand share, discount share, store concentration, basket shape) predicts its 4-week future spend beyond recent spend totals.
transformation_description: Added 30 product-mix and basket-shape features over trailing 84/112 days to E001's behavioural core: dept spend shares, dept spends, private-brand share, discount share, store count/concentration, product variety, repeat ratio, basket median/max/std, evening share, mix-shift.
reasoning_summary: Households buying different mixes (fresh vs drug/gas, private label, discount-driven) have different spending trajectories; these features add behavioural texture beyond totals.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is better predicted by the shape of a household's weekly spend trajectory (last 8 weeks incl. slope/variability), its monthly lag profile w3..w8 (persistence/seasonality of 28-day spend), zero-window patterns, gap statistics, and same-window-last-year spend than by trailing-window totals alone.
transformation_description: Added 37 temporal-dynamics features to E001's 18 behavioural features: weekly spend wk0..wk7 + weekly slope/std/active-weeks, monthly 28-day lags w3..w8, zero_frac_13/zero_streak, same-window-last-year spend + seasonal ratio, spend_7/14/21/168/252/504, trips/active_days over 84/168d, gap_prev/gap_mean_84.
reasoning_summary: Monthly lag windows and weekly trajectory shape capture autocorrelation and phase (households buy in cycles), which aggregate trailing totals miss; last-year same-window spend adds seasonality.

hypothesis: Long-run history structure adds signal beyond E004's recent-window features: year-ago same-window spend (seasonality), lifetime spend rate/tenure/regularity (weekly CV), inter-basket gap distribution (mean/median/max/std), basket shape (median/max basket value, lines, qty), shopping time-of-day, store concentration, and coupon redemptions predict future 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Added 31 long-run features to E004's 54: year-ago 4w/8w spend + ratio vs recent 28d, lifetime total/tenure/rate/active days-weeks/baskets/weekly CV, gap stats, basket median/max/lines/qty, hour/morning share, store count/top-store share, discount share, active weeks last 12w, redemptions total/84d.
reasoning_summary: E004 showed temporal dynamics beat product mix and marketing; year-ago spend captures seasonality, lifetime rate and gap structure capture stable spend propensity, and basket shape adds level information beyond spend totals.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is best predicted by the household's own lagged same-window spend profile: six consecutive non-overlapping trailing 28-day blocks (level, trend, variability, zero-block frequency) plus decay-weighted daily-spend EWMA levels beat overlapping trailing windows alone.
transformation_description: Added 23 features to E005's 85: spend in each of the 6 consecutive trailing 28-day blocks (raw + log1p), their mean/median/std/min/max/zero-count and latest-block ratio, plus half-life-14/28-day EWMA daily-spend annualised to 28 days (raw + log1p).
reasoning_summary: Lagged values of the target itself are its strongest predictors; explicit consecutive-block decomposition adds level, trend and variability signal beyond E005's overlapping windows and year-ago ratios.

hypothesis: The fixed evaluation model is linear, so heavy-tailed spend/count features (median-to-p95 spread > 4x) should be log1p-transformed to match the multiplicative structure of spend; this stabilises coefficients and improves validation MAE over E005.
transformation_description: Log1p-transformed the 57 heavy-tailed E005 features (spend blocks, weekly spends, gaps, life totals, ratios), leaving bounded/ratio features as-is.
reasoning_summary: Spend distributions are extremely heavy-tailed; a linear model on raw dollars is dominated by outliers and the 21% zero-spend rows, so log-scaling should reduce validation MAE.

hypothesis: The household's own forward-looking spend profile (EWMA of trailing 28-day blocks) plus calendar terms predicts future 4-week spend better than E005's window aggregates, because recent-block EWMA tracks level shifts faster than wide windows.
transformation_description: Added E006's forward-profile features (EWMA over trailing 28d blocks, block history, log variants) and 9 calendar features (day index, week-of-year, sin/cos harmonics, month index) to E005's 85 features.
reasoning_summary: Recent 28d blocks are the strongest single predictor; an EWMA over those blocks should capture the household level with less noise than 56/84/112d windows, and calendar terms capture seasonality that the fixed linear model cannot infer from raw day indices.

hypothesis: Demographic segments (household size, income level, age group, homeownership, kids) modulate a household's future 4-week spend beyond its behavioural history: segment main effects plus segment×log(spend-level) interactions let the fixed linear model fit segment-specific spend scales instead of one global level→future coefficient.
transformation_description: Added 24 features to E008's 115: ordinal codes for age/income/size/group/kids, one-hots for classification_2 and homeowner_desc, has_demo flag (zero-filled for the ~2/3 of households without demographics), plus interactions of each ordinal code with log1p(spend_84) and size×log1p(spend_28).
reasoning_summary: Household composition plausibly scales weekly spend (bigger families buy more), so segment×level interactions should sharpen level→future mapping; LOO proxy improved from 65.97 to 65.69.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is better predicted by a two-part structure (probability of any purchase × expected spend given active) than by raw spend levels alone: hinge-basis fitted conditional means decompose the ~20% zero-spend mass that linear terms on raw spend miss.
transformation_description: Added 45 two-part model features to E008's 117: hinge-basis regressions (basis in trailing 28d/84d/364d spend and EWMA blocks) predicting P(active) and E(spend|active), their product pred_2p, log variant, and per-window hazard rates hr_*; duplicates/constant columns dropped.
reasoning_summary: Decomposing spend into activity probability times conditional level may capture the zero-spend mass better than linear terms; locally it was tied-to-slightly-better than E008 on held-out train snapshot 431.

hypothesis: Price-promotion sensitivity (share of discounted items, discount $ rate, coupon use) and campaign-targeting exposure (type counts, recency, active flag) add predictive signal for 4-week spend beyond E009's behavioural+temporal+demo core; discount sensitivity also interacts with income/size.
transformation_description: Added 26 features to e009_demo (139): disc item-share & $-rate over 28/84/364d, retail vs coupon discount rates, coupon-user flag, log redemption counts (84/168/364d) + days-since-redemption, log campaign-target counts by TypeA/B/C + targeting recency/active/recent flags, and 3 discount×demo interactions.
reasoning_summary: Deal-seeking intensity is a stable household trait that shifts both purchase frequency and basket value, and campaign targeting plausibly changes near-term spend; E009 had redemptions but no discount-rate or targeting features.

hypothesis: Stock-up and trip-shape dynamics predict the next 4 weeks: a household whose last basket is unusually large relative to its 84-day norm (stock-up) will under-spend in the following 4 weeks, while high basket-value volatility and low unit price signal further stock-up cycles; trip timing (weekend/evening/morning shares) adds routine information.
transformation_description: Added 19 basket-shape features to e009_demo (139): last-basket value/lines/qty + log, basket mean/std/max over 84d, max basket in 28d, stock-up ratios (last/mean, max28/mean), basket CV, trips counts, qty28, unit price, and weekend/evening/morning trip shares.
reasoning_summary: E009's behavioural core lacks basket-level shape; stock-up cycles and trip routine are classic drivers of next-month spend and are orthogonal to the existing weekly-spend profile.

hypothesis: A household's future 4-week spend is better predicted by its own-history denoised central tendency (deviation of recent spend from its trailing same-window mean, weekly-spend CV, tenure-shrunk rates) and by explicit zero/tail-targeting transforms (dormancy hinges, weekly max/p90/top-2 concentration, within-snapshot rank transforms) than by E012's raw window aggregates alone.
transformation_description: Added 22 curated features to e012_basket_shape (158): own-history deviance ratios (c_dev28/c_dev84 vs trailing same-window means), 26-week spend CV, 7d-burst share, gap trend, stock-up concentration; zero/dormancy hinges (recency>45d, gap>30d, zero-frac>0.5); tail-targeting weekly max/p90/top-2 share; tenure-shrunk 28d/84d spend rates; and within-snapshot rank transforms of spend_28/spend_84/fwd28_mean/trips_28 plus sqrt and log² transforms of spend_28.
reasoning_summary: Residual analysis of the proxy model shows the biggest errors are underprediction of high spenders and overprediction of dormant/zero households; these features target exactly those regimes and were the only candidates with positive local-CV gains.

hypothesis: Market-level context improves prediction beyond household-level history: the average trailing-28d spend across all households at a snapshot (a market-level baseline that absorbs period drift), the market's 4-week momentum, and the household's spend relative to that market average carry signal that household-only features cannot capture. A shrunk (Empirical-Bayes style) household estimate — blending its trailing-28d spend toward the market median by trip frequency — adds a regularized level estimate.
transformation_description: Added 4 features to E013's 180: mkt28 (per-snapshot mean of trailing-28d spend across all households, observable within-snapshot), mkt_mom (ratio of consecutive snapshots' mkt28), drift28 (household spend_28 / mkt28), and shr (weighted blend of spend_28 toward the train median with weight trips_84/(trips_84+16)). All features computed from data observable at each snapshot; no target leakage (verified: shr uses only the global train median as a constant).
reasoning_summary: Pseudo-validation (holding out snapshots 347/375/403/431 from train) showed a consistent ~1.4 MAE improvement across every held-out snapshot and regularization strength, suggesting market-level drift and relative-position features capture a component of future spend that household-only history misses.

hypothesis: A nonlinear GBM's out-of-fold prediction of future_spend_4w captures interactions/nonlinearities in the 182 E013 features that the fixed linear model misses; adding it (plus a log variant) as two extra columns lets the linear model exploit that signal without changing the evaluation.
transformation_description: Added 2 features to E013's 182: gbm_pred and gbm_log = log1p(gbm_pred), where gbm_pred is a leak-free out-of-fold GBM prediction trained on the same 182 features (previously computed in E014's stacking work; per-snapshot OOF means are stable, unlike the earlier gbm_corr column).

hypothesis: A leak-free GBM's out-of-fold prediction of future_spend_4w captures nonlinearities/interactions the linear evaluation model misses; adding it as a stacker feature (scaled to ~O(1) so the linear model can weight it) improves validation MAE over E013.
transformation_description: Added 2 features to E013's 180: gbm_pred (out-of-fold GBM prediction from a snap-out CV, scaled /100) and gbm_log = log1p(gbm_pred*100)/100.
reasoning_summary: The GBM sees interactions and thresholds the linear model can't express; its OOF prediction is a denoised summary of all 180 features, so stacking it adds signal. Scaling avoids a huge coefficient dominating the fit. Proxy snap-out CV on train showed MAE 59.3 vs 60.75 for E013.

hypothesis: The fixed model is linear in the features, so representing each household's spend level with a hinge basis on log1p(spend) (piecewise-linear in log-space, capturing the concave MAE-optimal mapping from trailing spend to future spend) predicts future 4-week spend better than raw linear terms; and raw linear trend terms (day_idx) plus redundant long-run x_* features add noise that hurts generalization.
transformation_description: Added 30 hinge-basis features (max(0, log1p(spend_source) - quantile_k)) for 5 spend sources (spend_84, spend_28, fwd28_mean, wk_avg_84, spend_56) at 6 quantiles each, and dropped day_idx plus all 21 x_* long-run features from E015's 184 features (182 remain).
reasoning_summary: Local time-based ridge CV (validated against harness results on E013/E015) shows hinges on log-spend improve MAE ~0.1 and dropping day_idx/x_* improves ~0.2, combining to 63.28 vs 63.50 for E015 locally; the high-spend band carries 31% of MAE and is underpredicted, and a concave piecewise-linear-in-log mapping should fit it better.

hypothesis: Spend-level sources enter future 4-week spend nonlinearly with diminishing sensitivity, and marketing exposure adds signal: hinge bases on log1p of recency, spend_112/168, spend_rate_life, trips_84, spend_lag2, fwd28_median, active_days_28 plus display/mailer-exposure-weighted spend and coupon-redemption history improve on E018.
transformation_description: Added to E018's 182: 10 exposure features (exp84 mailer/display-weighted spend, lines, intensity; coupon redemptions; store diversity) + 48 hinge-basis features on 8 additional log-spend sources with train-quantile knots (kept sources with positive local gain).
reasoning_summary: E018's hinge trick was its biggest gain; extending hinges to recency and other spend sources (recency hinges showed the largest local improvement) and adding never-used display_mailer exposure context should capture nonlinear spend response and promo exposure.

hypothesis: Demographic segments (size, income, age, group, kids) modulate how strongly recent spend predicts future 4-week spend, and market-wide forward-looking spend context adds a small level signal: 40 interactions of 8 key spend features with 5 demographic ordinals plus a per-snapshot market mean of the forward-spend proxy.
transformation_description: Added to E019's 240 features: 40 interaction terms (spend_84, spend_28, wk_avg_8, fwd28_mean, ewma28_4w, spend_lag1, trips_84, spend_364 × size/income/age/group/kid ordinals) and mkt_fwd (per-snapshot market mean of fwd28_mean).
reasoning_summary: Interactions let the linear model capture that high-spend behaviour translates to future spend differently by household segment; the market forward mean adds a shared snapshot-level level shift.
